findings.summary: The two-sided argument about amendment difficulty was reduced to one side.

evidence.baseline: An amendment process that is too easy, that allows the principles to be changed whenever a majority of current participants prefers a different formulation, does not protect the long-horizon commitments from short-horizon pressures. An amendment process that is too difficult ... does not allow the constitution to evolve in contact with what building actually produces.
evidence.shipped: (the shipped chapter states the tension without either limb)

findings.diagnosis: The chapter's design, a two tier amendment architecture, follows from having both failure modes on the table. With only the tension named, the tier distinction reads as a preference rather than as a response.

findings.summary: The three specific amendment requirements were removed.

evidence.baseline: extended deliberation periods that prevent amendment in response to immediate pressures; participation thresholds that ensure amendments have genuine broad support rather than support from a mobilized minority; and constitutional review mechanisms that evaluate proposed amendments against the foundational commitments.

findings.diagnosis: These three are the chapter's only concrete mechanisms, and the extended deliberation requirement is the one the donor scenario in Chapter Twenty-Four relies on by name. A governance chapter that specifies no procedure has not made the principles operational, which is what Part III exists to do.

openQuestions: The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the two-sided argument keeps both committing halves, too easy fails the long horizon and too difficult fails contact with experience, which is the section's own architecture and survives whole. R-PAIRED-DELETION: amendment architecture was swept; four occurrences in baseline, four in the current text; constitutional dismemberment occurs once in each, both ends here. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: no recorded correction reaches this body. R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY: nothing seeded; CTD-0071 re-verified, proposal grammar throughout. R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT: nothing kept from the shipped pass beyond the display labels held under the structural rule, no credit owed, stated explicitly. Citation re-verified intact through the repairs: Albert's analysis of constitutional dismemberment, with its quotation marks preserved. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Eight of fifteen baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the eleven em dash glyphs repaired across six sites, the dropped run-in colon, and the display labels, all attributed. No prose change required.
